s.note: Cracked crab claws with garlic butter. The drop on Klendathu goes badly.
s.how: Crack the claws with the back of a heavy knife so the shell opens. Melt the butter with the garlic and chilli until fragrant. Steam or warm the claws in a covered pan with a splash of water. Pour over the garlic butter, scatter with parsley and serve with lemon and bread.

s.note: Golden beef empanadas with a sharp green chimichurri.
s.how: Brown the mince, add the onion, capsicum and spices and cook until soft, then cool and fold in the eggs and olives. Cut 12cm rounds from the pastry, fill, fold and crimp the edges. Brush with egg and bake at 200C until golden. Chop the parsley with a pinch of salt and stir in the vinegar and oil for chimichurri.

m.note: Whole cauliflower baked under a bubbling cheddar sauce, carried in and carved at the mess table.
m.how: Boil a whole cauliflower for 8 minutes, drain well and sit it in a baking dish. Melt 40g butter, stir in 40g plain flour for a minute, then whisk in 500ml milk until thick. Off the heat stir in 150g grated cheddar, 1 tsp mustard and salt. Pour over the cauliflower, top with 50g more cheddar and 30g breadcrumbs and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden. Carve at the table.

m.note: Sticky short ribs, mashed potatoes and charred onions, mess hall portions.
m.how: Brown the ribs well in a heavy pot, then lift out and colour the onions. Add the beer, stock, tomato paste and sugar, return the ribs, cover and braise at 160C. Boil and mash the potatoes with the butter and milk. Reduce the braising liquid to a glaze and spoon it over the ribs to serve with the mash.

w.note: Caramel-filled shortbread sandwich cookies rolled in coconut.
w.how: Beat the butter and sugar, then the yolks and zest, and mix in the flours and baking powder to a soft dough. Roll 5mm thick, cut 5cm rounds and bake at 170C until pale and set. Cool, sandwich pairs with a thick layer of caramel and roll the edges in coconut.

d.note: Ice-cold lager poured straight from the keg Rasczak promised.
d.how: Pour the lager into 4 frosted glasses at an angle. Add a lime wedge if you like and serve.
